summary: A remembered on/off boolean, driven by On / Off / Flip signals — the graph's toggle and one-bit memory.
description: Switch stores a single boolean state. The `on` (On), `off` (Off) and `flip` (Flip) signal inputs change it; `onFromStart` (State) is a boolean value input that sets the state directly and provides its initial value (default false). The current state is always readable on the `state` (Current State) boolean value output, and every state change also fires signals: `switched` (Switched) on any change, plus `switchedToOn` or `switchedToOff` matching the new state. `on` and `off` are ignored when the state already matches, so they never re-fire the signals; `flip` always changes state.
whenToUse: The idiomatic node for anything a user toggles: expand/collapse, mute, edit mode. Use `state` (a level) to drive `visible`/`enabled`-style inputs, and the switched signals only when something must happen at the moment of change. For more than two states use States; for deriving a boolean from data rather than events, use Condition or Expression.

ports.flip: Signal; inverts the state and always fires the switched signals.
ports.on: Signal; sets the state to true. Does nothing (and fires nothing) if it is already true.
ports.off: Signal; sets the state to false. Does nothing (and fires nothing) if it is already false.
ports.onFromStart: Boolean value (displayed as State); sets the state directly and defines the initial state. Changing it also fires the switched signals.
ports.state: Boolean value that always reflects the current state — wire this to `visible`/`enabled` style inputs.
ports.switched: Signal; fires on every state change, after `state` has been updated.
ports.switchedToOn: Signal; fires when a change leaves the state true.
ports.switchedToOff: Signal; fires when a change leaves the state false.

patterns: Button `onClick` → `flip`, `state` → a Group's `visible`: the standard show/hide toggle.
`state` → Boolean To String `input` → the toggling button's `label`: the button describes what it will do next.
antiPatterns: Wiring `switchedToOn` (a momentary signal) to a boolean input like `visible` — it delivers only a pulse; use `state` for anything that must stay on.
